note: Muscicapidae; Brown-chested Alethe. MalAvi files the genus under Turdidae, so the family pool matched Turdus poliocephalus, the Australasian Island Thrush. The records are African.
Passerellidae; clootl has the exact name (legacy key wrongly lumped it to Arremon torquatus)

Thraupidae; Oleaginous Hemispingus. Needed by hand because clootl no longer uses the genus Hemispingus, so the genus guard has nothing to check against; MalAvi's Fringillidae label had matched Crithagra frontalis, an African finch.

Muscicapidae; White-rumped Shama. clootl carries the Howard & Moore name 'Kittacincla malabarica' only on Copsychus albiventris, an Andaman endemic, so the synonym step resolved unambiguously to the wrong bird. The MalAvi records are from China.
Thraupidae; Greater Antillean Bullfinch. MalAvi's Fringillidae label had matched Euphonia violacea, a South American euphonia.
Oriolidae; MalAvi mislabels the family as Corvidae, which forced a false epithet-stem match to Corvus brachyrhynchos. clootl spells it brachyrynchus (one h)
Tyrannidae; eBird moved Phaeomyias into Nesotriccus. The Howard & Moore synonym 'Phaeomyias murina' is ambiguous (also on N. tumbezanus/maranonicus), so it must be set by hand to N. murinus
Pachycephalidae; a correct match that the genus guard declines, because clootl files Pitohui in Oriolidae and Pseudorectes in Pachycephalidae. Set by hand to keep it.
Pachycephalidae; as for Pitohui ferrugineus, a correct cross-family transfer the genus guard cannot distinguish from a false one.
Trochilidae; Green-crowned Woodnymph, treated by eBird/Clements within Crowned Woodnymph T. colombica. Without this the family-pool stem match wrongly hit Myrtis fanny (a woodstar)
Thraupidae; Blue-capped Tanager. MalAvi's Fringillidae label had matched Chlorophonia cyanocephala, the Golden-rumped Euphonia.
Thraupidae; Dull-colored Grassquit. MalAvi's Fringillidae label had matched Akialoa obscura, an extinct Hawaiian honeycreeper. Set by hand rather than left to the legacy key.
Leiothrichidae; White-throated Babbler. MalAvi's Timaliidae label had matched Mixornis gularis, the Pin-striped Tit-Babbler.
Parulidae; Blue-winged Warbler, renamed V. cyanoptera in 2010. The epithet match found Setophaga pinus, the Pine Warbler -- a different bird in the same family, which the genus guard cannot exclude.
Zosteropidae; capensis is a subspecies of Cape White-eye Z. virens under Clements. The legacy key carried the 2012 Jetz lump under Z. pallidus, Orange River White-eye.
